### Solution Steps:

1. **Projections of the Prism:**
   - Draw the top view as a regular pentagon with an edge of the base parallel to the $XY$ line (nearer to the observer/VP). Label the corners 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and corresponding top base corners as $1', 2', 3', 4', 5'$.
   - Project the front view as a rectangle of height $50\text{ mm}$ and base $25\text{ mm}$.

2. **Section Plane:**
   - Locate the center of the axis in the front view. Draw a section plane inclined at $45^\circ$ to the HP passing through this center point, perpendicular to the VP.

3. **(i) True Shape of Section:**
   - Project the intersection points obtained on the lateral edges and base edges perpendicularly onto a new reference line ($X_1Y_1$) drawn parallel to the section plane trace.
   - Measure the distances of respective points from the central axis in the top view and transfer them perpendicular to $X_1Y_1$ to obtain the true shape of the section.

4. **(ii) Development of Surfaces:**
   - Draw a straight stretch-out line equal to the perimeter of the pentagonal prism ($5 \times 25 = 125\text{ mm}$). Divide it into 5 equal parts of $25\text{ mm}$ each representing vertical edges.
   - Project the heights of the cut points from the front view horizontally onto the respective vertical generators on the development layout.
   - Join these points with straight lines to complete the development of the truncated pentagonal prism.
proTip: Always project true shapes perpendicular to the section line trace using divider measurements taken from the top view.
